definitions.explanation: A valuable item found at a surprisingly low price, or something unexpectedly good discovered among ordinary things. Often used when shopping at flea markets, thrift stores, or used goods shops.

examples.japanese: フリーマーケットで{掘|ほ}り{出|だ}し{物|もの}を{見|み}つけた。
examples.english: I found a bargain at the flea market.

examples.japanese: この{花瓶|かびん}は{掘|ほ}り{出|だ}し{物|もの}だった。100{円|えん}で{買|か}ったのに{本物|ほんもの}だ。
examples.english: This vase was a real find. I bought it for 100 yen, and it's the real thing.

examples.japanese: {中古|ちゅうこ}ショップを{回|まわ}れば、{掘|ほ}り{出|だ}し{物|もの}に{出会|であ}えることがある。
examples.english: If you visit secondhand shops, you can sometimes come across real bargains.

notes:
Literally "a dug-out thing" — like digging up buried treasure. The word conveys the excitement of finding something valuable that others overlooked.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {掘|ほ}り{出|だ}し{物|もの}を{見|み}つける (to find a bargain)
- {掘|ほ}り{出|だ}し{物|もの}に{出会|であ}う (to come across a treasure)
- {思|おも}わぬ{掘|ほ}り{出|だ}し{物|もの} (an unexpected find)

Often used at: フリーマーケット (flea markets), {骨董|こっとう}{市|いち} (antique fairs), {古本|ふるほん}{市|いち} (used book fairs), リサイクルショップ (thrift shops).
